findings.title: The promised public word-comparison/authority gate is not executable and the observer/restore control descriptions overstate their scope
evidence: eech-campaign/docs/d3-sector-height-production-contract.md sections7-9 and ACTIVE-EXTRACTION next_action promise a declared-window word-for-word comparison and controlled Host-change/withheld/malformed/wrong-sector/restoration witnesses.

The new entity-authority.lua phase17/18 branch parses and counts unaltered replies, but implements no height-input intervention/refusal mode and persists no Host-word stream for the promised comparison. The scripted tests generate17/18 themselves; they are not a native campaign witness.

The existing sector-height-baseline.lua requires observer feature methods. Its existing hooks have split scope after the move: SH2/3 raise and SH4/5 legacy save/restore hooks are inside original-only branches; SH10/11 still observe the now-Host-returned FIRST/fact12 word. Therefore the blanket claim that the observer observes no Host word is false, while a whole unchanged original-LINK report comparison is also invalid.

eech_sho.c clearance helper still reads raw->tallest_structure_height. That is retired storage in a hosted production build, not the Host getter value actually consumed by fw_move. It cannot supply M5 Host-input evidence if the guard is reached.

Contract section8 initially claims the real guarded fixed-wing expression is controlled, but its final named blocker correctly says no real-C or native control reaches the guards. The hosted control exercises the getter and actual pack/unpack over a scripted provider, not fw_move guarded execution.

Contract section7 includes restore-after-insertion among named refusals, but model_host.rs sector_height_event accepts a well-formed phase18 raw restore without an insertion-time guard; provider tests deliberately restore while placements are live. Restore-after-insertion must not be made invalid merely to satisfy that sentence.

production_source_assessment.ownership: One height word per sector lives in the existing SectorRoster heights map. The Host computes each arrival from stated canonical-record input and its own ModelStore scene box top; it does not accept a Core-computed height. This is not a second physical world/cache. The legacy member remains layout storage but has no authoritative hosted read/write; allocation zero-fill does not make it a second owner.
production_source_assessment.arrival_and_lifecycle: Per-sector-entry arrived tracks the first state statement under a newly issued sector key, including a building whose city-list record already held state. The accepted public callback order places that nested statement before LINK_CHILD. Later setters/restatements do not raise; removal does not lower; relink/new key gives a new arrival. City shape0 avoids a model read; a valid stated CITY shape can raise. The original fixed predicate is constant by the nine overload families, not a subtype or Corefalse bypass.
production_source_assessment.commit_safety: Statement words are classified by integer domain checks. The raise is computed before record mutation and applied only after set_fixed/set_city succeeds; arrived is then consumed once. The exclusive roster borrow prevents a concurrent entry change between these stages. Reads/restores validate facts/identity/sector before updating height. No query-time repair or old-field fallback is introduced.
production_source_assessment.writers_readers_reset: Reset clears height words before new sectors/entities. The hosted sc_msgs raise is excluded, sc_float getter issues phase17, sc_pack uses that getter and phase18 restoration before entity unpack order, and client/browse modes do not add height storage. Existing scan FIRST and guarded clearance expressions call the getter. Original solver profiles retain their explicit original bodies.
production_source_assessment.raw_protocol: C→Engine→Lua bridge→real provider→reply→C uses hex word transport for the raw height. C validates phase-specific state, exact3-word count, empty name, raw cursor echo, restore word echo and zero candidate tail before using output. Shared counts/states agree across C/sys/Engine/DC. Any malformed/refused response is fatal without fallback. Negative/Inf/qNaN histories remain raw; fact12 alone is exempted from finite classification and is bit-joined to the Host word for the candidate sector.
production_source_assessment.math_and_FP: The shared C expression retains one float addition and strict greater-than against the actual held word. ModelStore uses bounding_box[3], matching the established xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax/zmin/zmax transport. The kernel uses the existing model environment guard and caller restoration; controls cover rounding modes/caller masks/state and original-C result differentials. These are not a proof of original-vs-new internal sticky flags at every Core point, Windows execution, engine-C O2 or signalling-NaN behavior. No new concrete observable FP defect was established in this pass. No new RNG draw or campaign-policy/time change was found.
production_source_assessment.clean_code_boundary: The scalar remains in the existing roster/store/kernel architecture; no second ABI, service process or generic framework was added. Fixed/CITY stage-specific handling and integer transport remain bounded. Map absence represents fresh-sector zero as declared; the Host lacks a world-map validity catalogue, so it must not claim exhaustive geography validation.
production_source_assessment.required_remaining_coupling: Static poses, shape provenance, source/target exclusion, hierarchy/model consumers and other all-ten D3 requirements remain explicit. The finite scalar move does not waive guarded clearance/native save/restore or final compiled-consumer census.
